_about: What the city take's model happened to write, remarked on where it is read (build_storyboard.py, REST_NOTES once use() points at the city take; "p<i>" after passage i, counted without the judges' letters). Rewritten for each retake. Take: build/rec_city.
fight_2_end: Look at what the first thrust did. It broke the wolf's backbone, and the backbone is where movement comes from. From then on the wolf had no points left to act with, and it never struck back once. Where you hit matters.
p2: Provisioning frets about salt we do not even carry. A will sees the world through what it wants, and this one wants supplies, so it finds a shortage everywhere. Read it as the character's own anxious habit.
p4: The outcome runs a little ahead of itself: nothing is bought yet. What the act secured is the meeting. The purchase is still a conversation away.
p5: A quest, he asks. There are no quests in this game; read it as a cobbler hoping we bring him business.
p13: His answer wanders into a riddle. The fixed meaning underneath is plain enough: some of the cheap stock is good.
p21: He admits he once sold us the wrong thing, twice. A frank cobbler, or a careless one. Either way, the tree has reached its end.
advice_proposing: My advice: dress for the people you deal with. Here the townsman's clothes alone gave four dice.
p22: More silver beneath the world's crust: a good trade, felt as buried treasure.
